title: Psalms Chapter 104 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 104 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 104 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 104.

questions.question: What does the psalmist declare about the LORD in Psalms 104:1?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, 'O LORD my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty.' (Psalms 104:1)

questions.question: According to Psalms 104:2, how does the LORD cover Himself?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that the LORD 'coverest thyself with light as with a garment.' (Psalms 104:2)

questions.question: What does Psalms 104:4 say about the angels of the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Who maketh his angels spirits.' (Psalms 104:4)

questions.question: Which of the following does the LORD do according to Psalms 104:3?
options: Walk upon the wings of the wind
questions.correctAnswer: Walk upon the wings of the wind
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'who walketh upon the wings of the wind.' (Psalms 104:3)

questions.question: In Psalms 104:6, what did the LORD cover the earth with?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions, 'Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment.' (Psalms 104:6)

questions.question: True or False: The waters stood above the mountains according to Psalms 104:6.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'the waters stood above the mountains.' (Psalms 104:6)

questions.question: What happens at the LORD's rebuke according to Psalms 104:7?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'At thy rebuke they fled.' (Psalms 104:7)

questions.question: True or False: The wild asses quench their thirst according to Psalms 104:11.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'the wild asses quench their thirst.' (Psalms 104:11)

questions.question: What do the fowls of heaven do by the trees according to Psalms 104:12?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions, 'which sing among the branches.' (Psalms 104:12)

questions.question: According to Psalms 104:13, what does the LORD water?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He watereth the hills from his chambers.' (Psalms 104:13)

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 104:5 states that the foundations of the earth should be removed forever.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'that it should not be removed for ever.' (Psalms 104:5), indicating it should remain.

questions.question: In what manner does the LORD stretch out the heavens according to Psalms 104:2?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain.' (Psalms 104:2)

questions.question: What is set by the LORD in Psalms 104:9?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions, 'Thou hast set a bound that they may not pass over.' (Psalms 104:9)

questions.question: True or False: The young lions seek their prey from man according to Psalms 104:21.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'and seek their meat from God.' (Psalms 104:21), indicating they seek from God, not man.

questions.question: In Psalms 104, what comes first according to the order of the verses?
options: The foundations of the earth are laid
The wild asses quench their thirst
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with the psalmist praising the LORD in verse 1: 'Bless the LORD, O my soul.' (Psalms 104:1)

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 104 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 104 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Psalms 104:13 say God does for the hills?
options: He watereth the hills from his chambers
questions.correctAnswer: He watereth the hills from his chambers
questions.explanation: This is stated in Psalms 104:13, which describes how God waters the hills, highlighting His provision for the earth.

questions.question: What does God cause to grow for the cattle according to Psalms 104:14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:14 explicitly states that God causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, showing His care for creation.

questions.question: According to Psalms 104:15, what does wine do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:15 mentions that wine maketh glad the heart of man, illustrating the blessings God provides.

questions.question: What do the trees of the LORD provide according to Psalms 104:16?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:16 states that the trees of the LORD are full of sap, indicating their vitality and purpose.

questions.question: According to Psalms 104:18, where do wild goats find refuge?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:18 describes the high hills as a refuge for wild goats, demonstrating God's provision for wildlife.

questions.question: What is appointed for seasons in Psalms 104:19?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:19 states that God appointed the moon for seasons, highlighting His control over time and nature.

questions.question: What happens at night according to Psalms 104:20?
options: The beasts of the forest creep forth
questions.correctAnswer: The beasts of the forest creep forth
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:20 explains that at night, all the beasts of the forest do creep forth, indicating the cycle of creation.

questions.question: True or False: The young lions seek their meat from humans according to Psalms 104:21.
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:21 states that young lions seek their meat from God, not from humans, emphasizing dependence on God.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 104:23 states that man goes forth to his work until evening.
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:23 confirms that man goeth forth unto his work and to his labour until the evening, reflecting the nature of human effort.

questions.question: What does Psalms 104:24 praise about God's creation?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:24 declares that the earth is full of God's riches, showcasing His abundant provision.

questions.question: What do the creatures wait for in Psalms 104:27?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:27 mentions that creatures wait upon God to give them their meat in due season, highlighting their reliance on Him.

questions.question: What happens when God hides His face according to Psalms 104:29?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:29 states that when God hides His face, they are troubled, indicating their dependence on His presence.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 104:30 teaches that God's spirit is involved in creation.
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:30 confirms that God's spirit is involved in creation, as it states, 'Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created.'

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 104 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 104.

questions.question: What does the verse Psalms 104:25 say about the sea?
options: It is great and wide, filled with beasts.
It is dangerous and full of storms.
questions.correctAnswer: It is great and wide, filled with beasts.
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:25 states, 'So is this great and wide sea, wherein are things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts.' This highlights the vastness and diversity of life within the sea.

questions.question: According to Psalms 104:27, what do all creatures wait for?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:27 states, 'These wait all upon thee; that thou mayest give them their meat in due season,' indicating that all creatures rely on God for their food.

questions.question: Which creature is mentioned in Psalms 104:26 as playing in the sea?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:26 mentions, 'There go the ships: there is that leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein,' referring to the leviathan as a creature of the sea.

questions.question: What does Psalms 104:30 say God sends forth to create life?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:30 states, 'Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth,' indicating that God's spirit is responsible for creation.

questions.question: What happens when God hides His face according to Psalms 104:29?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:29 states, 'Thou hidest thy face, they are troubled,' showing that the absence of God's presence causes distress.

questions.question: The glory of the LORD is said to endure for how long in Psalms 104:31?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:31 states, 'The glory of the LORD shall endure for ever,' emphasizing the eternal nature of God's glory.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 104:34 expresses a desire to be glad in the LORD.
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:34 states, 'My meditation of him shall be sweet: I will be glad in the LORD,' affirming the joy found in God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 104:22, what do the young lions do when the sun arises?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:22 states, 'The sun ariseth, they gather themselves together, and lay them down in their dens,' indicating that they rest after hunting.

questions.question: What does Psalms 104:35 say should happen to sinners and the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:35 states, 'Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more,' calling for the removal of evil.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently featured in Psalms 104 regarding the relationship between God and creation?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104 utilizes parallelism in its poetic structure, presenting complementary ideas that enhance the depiction of God's works throughout creation.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 104:20 mentions that all beasts of the forest come out during the day.
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:20 states, 'Thou makest darkness, and it is night: wherein all the beasts of the forest do creep forth,' indicating that they come out at night, not during the day.

questions.question: Which theme from Psalms 104 connects with Genesis 1:30 regarding God's provision for all creatures?
questions.explanation: Both Psalms 104 and Genesis 1:30 emphasize God's provision for all creatures, highlighting His role as the Creator who provides sustenance.

questions.question: In which verse does the concept of God renewing the earth appear, resonating with Isaiah 40:31?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:30 states, 'Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth,' paralleling God's renewing work mentioned in Isaiah 40:31.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 104 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 104 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 104:1 reveal about the nature of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:1 states, 'O LORD my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty,' indicating God's greatness as a central attribute.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is illustrated by Him covering Himself with light in Psalms 104:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:2 describes God as covering Himself with light, illustrating His majestic nature.

questions.question: In Psalms 104:5, what is emphasized about the foundations of the earth?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:5 says, 'Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever,' emphasizing God's role in creation.

questions.question: What role do the clouds serve according to Psalms 104:3?
options: They are a source of rain
They are a sign of storms
They are a form of judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:3 states, 'who maketh the clouds his chariot,' indicating that clouds serve the divine purpose as God's chariot.

questions.question: What insight does Psalms 104:10 provide about the natural world?
options: They are a source of destruction
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:10 indicates that 'He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills,' showing the natural order of creation.

questions.question: What do Psalms 104:14-15 reveal about God's provision for humanity?
options: He provides only for the rich
He does not care for humanity
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:14-15 states, 'He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man: that he may bring forth food out of the earth,' showing God's provision.

questions.question: How does Psalms 104:27-28 address the dependence of creation on God?
options: Creation waits upon God for sustenance
Creation does not rely on God
questions.correctAnswer: Creation waits upon God for sustenance
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:27-28 explains that 'These wait all upon thee; that thou mayest give them their meat in due season,' indicating creation's reliance on God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 104:24 teach about the wisdom of God in creation?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:24 states, 'O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all,' highlighting God's wisdom in creation.

questions.question: What does the reference to the 'leviathan' in Psalms 104:26 signify?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:26 mentions 'leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein,' signifying God's power in creating even the most formidable beings.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 29 and 30 convey about life and death?
options: God gives and takes away breath
Death is not part of creation
questions.correctAnswer: God gives and takes away breath
questions.explanation: Verses 29 and 30 together show that 'Thou hidest thy face, they are troubled: thou takest away their breath, they die,' demonstrating God's sovereignty over life and death.

questions.question: How does Psalms 104:32 illustrate God's power over creation?
options: The earth trembles at His look
Creation is immune to His influence
God has no control over the earth
The earth is indifferent to Him
questions.correctAnswer: The earth trembles at His look
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:32 states, 'He looketh on the earth, and it trembleth,' emphasizing God's immense power and authority over creation.

questions.question: What does the final verse of Psalms 104 teach about the worship of God?
options: The soul should bless the LORD
Praise is only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: The soul should bless the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:35 concludes with 'Bless thou the LORD, O my soul. Praise ye the LORD,' emphasizing the call to worship and bless God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 104:21 reveal about God's provision for animals?
options: He provides for even the young lions
Animals are not a part of creation
questions.correctAnswer: He provides for even the young lions
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:21 states, 'The young lions roar after their prey, and seek their meat from God,' showing God's provision extends to all of creation.

questions.question: How does Psalms 104:18 reflect God's care for all creatures?
options: High hills are a refuge for wild goats
God only cares for the mighty
questions.correctAnswer: High hills are a refuge for wild goats
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:18 mentions, 'The high hills are a refuge for the wild goats,' illustrating God's provision and care for all creatures.

questions.question: What does the appointment of the moon in Psalms 104:19 signify about God's sovereignty over time?
questions.explanation: Psalms 104:19 states, 'He appointed the moon for seasons,' indicating God's sovereignty and authority over time and creation.
